title: Design System: 東京近郊即時影像 · 車站告示系統

led-off.note: JS constant OFF in the LED renderer, not a CSS custom property.

amber.note: Also JS constants AMB/GRN/RED; LIFT/SHADE tables are keyed by this hex.

green.note: Also JS constants AMB/GRN/RED; LIFT/SHADE tables are keyed by this hex.

red.note: Also JS constants AMB/GRN/RED; LIFT/SHADE tables are keyed by this hex.

station-name.purpose: Kanji on a 駅名標; kana 12px .2em above, romaji below.

line-head.purpose: Region name over its 6px line-colour rule.

title.purpose: Page title in the top bar, with a Hind romaji subtitle.

poster-head.purpose: White heading in a navy 案内 head; Japanese sign term 11px .12em beside it.

caption.purpose: Camera place name on its sign strip (13.5px below 700px).

small.purpose: Hints, sources, secondary lines in plate-2.

figure.purpose: Temperatures and readings, tabular Hind (20px on the sign, 15px road readings).

led.purpose: GNU Unifont 8×16 / 16×16 bitmaps from the LEDG table, drawn on canvas; rebuild with tools/led-glyphs.py. Not a CSS font.

shadows.name: lamp-rim
shadows.purpose: Rim of a Fuji status lamp; the only box-shadow in the system.

shadows.name: bracket
shadows.value: ::before 4×14px post + ::after 38×4px bar in housing-2 above each monitor (14px top padding)
shadows.purpose: Hangs each ITV monitor; depth by mounting, not shadow.

motion.name: led-pitch
motion.value: --led-pitch 1.3 CSS px per dot (2 at ≥1100px); dp = round(pitch × devicePixelRatio)

motion.name: led-dot-rules
motion.value: dp ≥ 3: lit dot dp − max(1, floor(dp/4)) with gap; dp 2: shade cell + one bright pixel; dp 1: solid; unlit #24221f square of dp − 1 under every cell
motion.purpose: Keep the dot grid visible and the LED bright at every density.

motion.name: led-scroll
motion.value: one rAF clock, 1 dot-column per 42ms (24/s), whole-dot steps, 40-column loop gap; paused on hover/touch, off-screen and hidden tab
motion.purpose: Long route steps and the weather ticker.

motion.name: board-wipe
motion.value: 7 columns per 16ms from the left, each row delayed 24ms × row index
motion.purpose: Day change redraws the board column by column.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: no scrolling (rows wrap with CJK line-break rules), no wipe, weather defaults to the table, smooth scroll off

motion.name: signs-static
motion.value: no CSS transitions or animations anywhere
motion.purpose: Signs, panels and monitors never animate.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Station Concourse"**

The page is a Japanese railway station. You walk in through a yellow 出口 sign and reach a black LED departure board (発車標) that shows the day's itinerary in dot-matrix light. Beside it are the station's 運行情報 displays: navy-headed enamel panels that carry the weather, the Fuji lamps, the speed-limit notice and the current picks. Further down the concourse every camera area gets a white 駅名標 standing on its own line. Each sign has a line-colour band, a ringed station-number badge, the name in kana, kanji and romaji, and the previous and next stations. The area's cameras hang below the sign from brackets, like platform ITV monitors.

Everything is signage. Surfaces are flat enamel, painted housing or lit LED. Depth comes from objects hanging and standing (a bracket, a housing, a sign edge), never from soft shadows. Only the LED board moves, and it moves in LED grammar: whole-dot steps, column-by-column wipes, hard on and off. The signs never animate.

Confirmed rejection, from the direction contract: the category default of a dark CCTV wall made of same-size thumbnail cards under a hero. In this world the monitors belong to the station signs; they never form a free-standing grid of cards.
keyCharacteristics: A station's three kinds of signage: an LED board for time-bound plans, navy-headed enamel panels for status, white 駅名標 for places.
LED text is real dot matrix: GNU Unifont 16-dot bitmaps drawn dot by dot on canvas, with the unlit dots visible.
Four line colours (TK / YS / HF / IZ) are the page's own grouping and the only chromatic accents on the signs.
Filled JIS-style pictograms from one inline SVG sprite; no outline icon sets, no emoji.
Night platform in dark mode: the concourse and panels go dark, the 駅名標 and exit sign stay lit.

rules.name: The Signs Stay Lit Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is a station at night. `ground`, `plate` and the status inks change, and `navy` lifts to `#2a3a5c`. The 駅名標 (`sign`, which dims only to `#ecebe6`), the exit sign, the badges, the number plates and the LED housing keep their colours. A dark-mode screen still shows white station signs.

rules.name: The Three LEDs Rule
rules.body: An LED shows amber, green or red and nothing else. Green names (titles, times, cities), amber informs (steps, readings), red warns (notes, deadlines, a wet rain chance). The JS constants `AMB / GRN / RED` and the `LIFT` / `SHADE` tables are keyed by these exact hex values, so a new LED colour needs all three tables updated, not just the CSS token.

rules.name: The Line Is the Accent Rule
rules.body: Line colours appear only as signage geometry: bands, rules, rings and the route track. They never fill a panel or set body text.

rules.name: The Bilingual Sign Rule
rules.body: Place names are written the way a station writes them: kana over kanji over romaji on the 駅名標, a romaji line under the next- and previous-station names, and the Japanese sign term set after a poster head. The second language always sits **beside or below** its name in the same object. It never floats above a heading as a label of its own.

rules.name: The Lit Text Is Bitmap Rule
rules.body: Anything shown on the LED board, the board clocks or the weather ticker is drawn from Unifont bitmaps on canvas, with a screen-reader copy in a `.sr` span next to it. After changing any text the board can show, run `tools/led-glyphs.py`. A character missing from the table is rasterised from the browser font at 16px as a fallback, so it still renders, only less crisply.

rules.name: The Hung, Not Lifted Rule
rules.body: If an object needs to read as separate from the concourse, mount it: a bracket, a housing edge or a sign rule. Don't use blur shadows, glow or hover lifts. Hover changes are underline, border colour or a flat background swap.

dos: Do put time-bound plans on the LED board, status on navy-headed 案内 panels, and places on white 駅名標. Each kind of information has its own kind of signage.
Do draw every lit character from the Unifont table on canvas with its unlit dots, keep a `.sr` text copy beside it, and re-run `tools/led-glyphs.py` after changing board text.
Do keep LED colours to amber, green and red with their meanings (green names, amber informs, red warns), and update `AMB/GRN/RED`, `LIFT` and `SHADE` together.
Do move LEDs only in whole-dot steps or column wipes, pause scrolling on hover, touch and off-screen, and wrap instead of scrolling under reduced motion.
Do carry a region's line colour through `--line` on its bands, rules, rings and route track, and give every new area a badge code on its line (TK05, YS03…).
Do hang every camera from its bracket with a hood number plate (`LINE` + number + `-` + index) and a separate caption sign strip.
Do keep the 駅名標, exit sign, badges and housings lit in dark mode; only the concourse, panels and status inks change.
Do use the filled pictogram sprite for every icon, at 1em in `currentColor`.
donts: Don't lay the cameras out as a free-standing wall of same-size thumbnail cards under a hero; monitors always hang under their station sign.
Don't animate signs, panels or monitors: no fades, slides, hover lifts or easing. Motion belongs to the LED board alone.
Don't add blur shadows, glow or gradients; separation is a bracket, a housing edge or a 1px rule.
Don't set LED text in a CSS web font or invent a fourth LED colour.
Don't fill panels or set body text in line colours, or present TK / YS / HF / IZ as real railway lines.
Don't float the second-language term above a heading as a label; it sits beside or below its name.
Don't use emoji or outline icon sets.
